page.layout: One printed page: a woodcut diagram of concentric celestial spheres with zodiac and planet signs at top; below it a centred heading in large type, then a paragraph of text in full lines; a signature line at the foot right. No margin notes. The digitiser's banner at the bottom is left out.

main_text.head: Quod orbium coelestium duo sint primi motus.
main_text.p: ETSI orbes coelestes proprijs singuli et dissi-milibus agitantur motibus, duos tamen primos tan-tum esse motus cum obseruationibus, tum sensuum iudicio constat. Vnus est, quo omnes orbes ab ortu in occasum circa polos mundi, seu aequatoris ἀεὶ ὠκ-ύτως καὶ ἰσοταχῶς, id est, aequali perpetuo celeritate uecti circulis aequatori parallelis, spa-tio

page.notes: The Greek phrase in the last lines is reproduced as far as legible; the words "ἀεὶ ὠκ-ύτως" and "ἰσοταχῶς" are doubtful in the scan. The woodcut diagram is not transcribed as text. The printed signature at the foot reads "E 2" and the word "clo" stands beside it, probably the start of a date or a printed fragment; it is uncertain. The last word of the paragraph, "spa-", is a line-end hyphenation and the continuation is cut off at the page foot. The running head is absent.
